scan.method: Common RIP MOV references, PE-range prefix alignment, bounded 512-byte/96-instruction lookahead; field displacement is a lead, not alias proof
limits: Common MOV RIP patterns only; not exhaustive xrefs.
512-byte / 96-instruction root lookahead is not alias analysis.
Disp32 byte-operand scan requires a PE range and prefix <=65536 bytes; decode may stop on data.
One store at 0x8afbc8 is unassociated byte-array code; matching offsets do not identify objects.

findings.claim: String-associated settings update stores +0x146 and sets byte +0x18 bit3; UI reads +0x146.
Event branch checks accessed settings byte +0x146; accessor has component-associated and global-root fallback paths.
Two event integers feed a segment-producing path; endpoint uses scalar 100; successful query output supplies 12 bytes to setter.
Setter calls follow-stop and destination-clearing routines, writes 12 bytes at state=[receiver+0xb90], +0x60/+0x68, and sets state byte +0x1a8 bit0.
Consumer tests same bit, reads +0x60/+0x68, may create state+0x70 handle, computes position deltas and squared distance, reaches orientation-like calls and near-distance clearing.
This event-to-segment-to-query-to-active-vector chain is a native C2M destination path. Pixel/button meanings, coordinate frame, current-player ownership and actual runtime behavior remain unproven.

historicalEvidence.claim: Later probe rejected player-centered +/-40 box as fixed destination; subsequent fixed-goal scan found zero qualifying goals.
Reports July C2M movement and waypoint arrivals; not a current-build isolated-native-routing proof.
Foreground SendInput, W2S/center aim, repeated re-aim/detours and optional default-on A/D presteps; planned-goal arrival check rather than native-destination read.

limitations: No live experiment: no gameplay success, stopping success or route validity claimed.

Receiver identity/current-player root and component/global settings equivalence unproven.
